title: Home inspector lead disclosure: what sellers, landlords and agents must do practice questions
description: Practice questions on federal lead disclosure duties for pre-1978 housing: pamphlet, records, 10-day evaluation, attachments, agents (40 CFR 745).

questions.question: A seller of a 1962 house has never had it tested for lead. The buyer's friend says the seller must have a lead inspection done and fix any hazards before the buyer signs. What does 745.107(a) say about this?

options.A: The seller must have a lead-based paint inspection done before listing the house
options.B: Nothing in 745.107 implies a positive obligation on the seller or lessor to conduct any evaluation or reduction activities
options.C: The seller must complete reduction of any hazards within 10 days after the contract
options.D: The seller must order a risk assessment if the purchaser asks for one

questions.explanation: 745.107(a) says: "Nothing in this section implies a positive obligation on the seller or lessor to conduct any evaluation or reduction activities."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.107, Disclosure requirements for sellers and lessors (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: A seller is putting together the lead disclosure packet for a buyer. Under 745.107(a)(1), which of these may be given as the required lead hazard information pamphlet?

options.A: A lead safety brochure written by the listing agent's brokerage
options.B: A State home inspector licensing handbook
options.C: A copy of a lead-based paint inspection report prepared for the property
options.D: An equivalent pamphlet that has been approved for use in that State by EPA

questions.explanation: The seller or lessor "shall provide the purchaser or lessee with an EPA-approved lead hazard information pamphlet." Such pamphlets include Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home "or an equivalent pamphlet that has been approved for use in that State by EPA."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.107, Disclosure requirements for sellers and lessors (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: A seller in multifamily target housing has an available report on lead-based paint in the building's hallways and stairways. Under 745.107(a)(4), how is that report treated?

options.A: It is part of the records or reports the seller shall provide to the purchaser, because the requirement includes records or reports regarding common areas
options.B: It is kept by the seller, because only reports on the unit being sold must be provided
options.C: It is sent to EPA instead of to the purchaser
options.D: It is given only if the purchaser asks for it in writing

questions.explanation: 745.107(a)(4) requires the seller or lessor to provide available records or reports, and "This requirement includes records or reports regarding common areas." Hallways and stairways are among the common areas listed in the 745.103 definition.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.107, Disclosure requirements for sellers and lessors (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: A purchaser makes an offer on target housing before the seller has given the required disclosures. What does 745.107(b) require the seller to do?

options.A: Accept the offer first and give the disclosures within 10 days
options.B: Give the disclosures at closing together with the deed
options.C: Complete the required disclosure activities before accepting the offer, and allow the purchaser an opportunity to review the information and possibly amend the offer
options.D: Reject the offer and ask the purchaser to make a new one after an inspection

questions.explanation: The seller or lessor "shall complete the required disclosure activities prior to accepting the purchaser's or lessee's offer and allow the purchaser or lessee an opportunity to review the information and possibly amend the offer."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.107, Disclosure requirements for sellers and lessors (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: Under 745.107(a)(3), what must the seller or lessor disclose to each agent?

options.A: The presence of any known lead-based paint and/or lead-based paint hazards and the existence of any available records or reports pertaining to them
options.B: Only whether the housing was built before 1978
options.C: Only the results of a risk assessment the seller ordered for the sale
options.D: The purchaser's offer price and financing terms

questions.explanation: The seller or lessor "shall disclose to each agent the presence of any known lead-based paint and/or lead-based paint hazards" and "the existence of any available records or reports pertaining to lead-based paint and/or lead-based paint hazards."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.107, Disclosure requirements for sellers and lessors (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: A listing agent finds that the seller of a 1955 house knows nothing about the federal lead disclosure duties. To ensure compliance, what does 745.115(a) say the agent shall do?

options.A: Have a lead-based paint inspection done before the house is listed
options.B: Report the seller to EPA and take no further part in the disclosure
options.C: Inform the seller of his/her obligations under 745.107, 745.110 and 745.113, and ensure the seller has performed the required activities or personally ensure compliance
options.D: Wait until the purchaser asks about lead before raising the subject

questions.explanation: To ensure compliance, the agent shall "Inform the seller or lessor of his/her obligations under §§ 745.107, 745.110, and 745.113" and "Ensure that the seller or lessor has performed all activities required under §§ 745.107, 745.110, and 745.113, or personally ensure compliance with the requirements of §§ 745.107, 745.110, and 745.113."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.115, Agent responsibilities (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: An agent has complied with 745.115(a)(1). The seller knew of lead-based paint hazards, did not tell the agent, and did not disclose them to the purchaser. What does 745.115(b) say about the agent?

options.A: The agent is liable in the same way as the seller
options.B: The agent shall not be liable for the failure to disclose hazards known by the seller but not disclosed to the agent
options.C: The agent is liable unless EPA excuses the agent in writing
options.D: The agent is liable only if the agent signed the contract attachment

questions.explanation: If the agent has complied with 745.115(a)(1), "the agent shall not be liable for the failure to disclose to a purchaser or lessee the presence of lead-based paint and/or lead-based paint hazards known by a seller or lessor but not disclosed to the agent."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.115, Agent responsibilities (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: Before signing, a buyer and seller of target housing put in writing that the buyer will have 14 days, not 10, for a lead risk assessment or inspection. What does 745.110(a) say about the evaluation period?

options.A: A period other than 10 days is allowed only with EPA's approval
options.B: The period may be shortened by agreement, but never lengthened
options.C: The period is always exactly 10 days, whatever the parties agree
options.D: It is a 10-day period unless the parties mutually agree, in writing, upon a different period of time

questions.explanation: The seller "shall permit the purchaser a 10-day period (unless the parties mutually agree, in writing, upon a different period of time)" to conduct a risk assessment or inspection.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.110, Opportunity to conduct an evaluation (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: A seller's agent is preparing the sales contract attachment for a house built in 1950. Which sentence is part of the Lead Warning Statement that 745.113(a)(1) requires?

options.A: Lead poisoning poses a risk only to children under 6 years of age.
options.B: Lead poisoning in young children is always temporary.
options.C: Lead-based paint in good condition must be removed before closing.
options.D: Lead poisoning also poses a particular risk to pregnant women.

questions.explanation: 745.113(a)(1) requires a Lead Warning Statement whose language includes: "Lead poisoning in young children may produce permanent neurological damage, including learning disabilities, reduced intelligence quotient, behavioral problems, and impaired memory. Lead poisoning also poses a particular risk to pregnant women."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.113, Certification and acknowledgment of disclosure (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: A cash buyer of a 1950s house plans to strip and repaint every room and does not want a lead risk assessment or inspection. What does 745.110(b) say the buyer may do?

options.A: Waive the opportunity to conduct the risk assessment or inspection by so indicating in writing
options.B: Skip the evaluation only if the seller agrees to lower the price
options.C: Nothing; the risk assessment or inspection must be done before closing
options.D: Ask EPA to grant a waiver of the evaluation

questions.explanation: 745.110(b) says "a purchaser may waive the opportunity to conduct the risk assessment or inspection by so indicating in writing."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.110, Opportunity to conduct an evaluation (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: A seller has no records or reports on lead-based paint or hazards in the housing. What does 745.113(a)(3) say the seller shall do on the attachment?

options.A: Leave the records list off the attachment
options.B: Have an evaluation done so that a report can be listed
options.C: So indicate, since no such records or reports are available
options.D: Ask the agent to sign the list in place of the seller

questions.explanation: The attachment includes a list of available records or reports provided to the purchaser, and "If no such records or reports are available, the seller shall so indicate."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.113, Certification and acknowledgment of disclosure (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: In the sales attachment, 745.113(a)(2) is the seller's disclosure statement and 745.113(a)(3) is the list of available records or reports. What does the purchaser's statement required by 745.113(a)(4) affirm?

options.A: Completion of a lead-based paint inspection of the housing
options.B: Receipt of the information set out in 745.113(a)(2) and (3) and the lead hazard information pamphlet
options.C: Receipt of a lead-based paint free certificate from the seller
options.D: Payment for a risk assessment ordered by the seller

questions.explanation: 745.113(a)(4) requires "A statement by the purchaser affirming receipt of the information set out in paragraphs (a)(2) and (3) of this section and the lead hazard information pamphlet required under 15 U.S.C. 2686."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.113, Certification and acknowledgment of disclosure (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: Whose signatures does 745.113(a)(7) require on the sales attachment?

options.A: The sellers, agents, and purchasers, certifying to the accuracy of their statements to the best of their knowledge, with the dates of signature
options.B: The seller only, with the date of signature
options.C: The seller and an EPA representative
options.D: The purchaser and the home inspector who examined the property

questions.explanation: 745.113(a)(7) requires "The signatures of the sellers, agents, and purchasers certifying to the accuracy of their statements to the best of their knowledge, along with the dates of signature."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.113, Certification and acknowledgment of disclosure (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: How does 745.113(b) say the required elements must be included in a contract to lease target housing?

options.A: Only as a separate attachment, always written in English
options.B: As an attachment or within the contract, in the language of the contract
options.C: In a separate letter given after the lessee moves in
options.D: In a notice filed with EPA instead of in the contract

questions.explanation: Each contract to lease target housing "shall include, as an attachment or within the contract, the following elements, in the language of the contract (e.g., English, Spanish)".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.113, Certification and acknowledgment of disclosure (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.question: A landlord is drafting the Lead Warning Statement for a lease of a 1965 apartment. Which sentence does 745.113(b)(1) put in that statement?

options.A: Lessees must be given a 10-day period to conduct a risk assessment or inspection.
options.B: Lessors must have the unit inspected for lead before each new lease.
options.C: Lessees must sign a waiver of lead testing before moving in.
options.D: Lessees must also receive a federally approved pamphlet on lead poisoning prevention.

questions.explanation: The lease Lead Warning Statement ends: "Before renting pre-1978 housing, lessors must disclose the presence of known lead-based paint and/or lead-based paint hazards in the dwelling. Lessees must also receive a federally approved pamphlet on lead poisoning prevention."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.113, Certification and acknowledgment of disclosure (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.topic: Keeping records, forms and electronic disclosure
questions.question: A lessor and lessee sign a two-year lease of a 1960 apartment, and the leasing period begins July 1, 2026. Under 745.113(c)(1), the lessor keeps a copy of the completed lease disclosure for no less than 3 years counted from when?

options.A: From June 30, 2028, when the leasing period ends
options.B: From the day the lessee moves out
options.C: From July 1, 2026, the commencement of the leasing period
options.D: From the day the lessor first advertised the unit

questions.explanation: The lessor, and any agent, shall retain a copy of the completed attachment or lease contract "for no less than 3 years from the commencement of the leasing period."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.113, Certification and acknowledgment of disclosure (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.topic: Keeping records, forms and electronic disclosure
questions.question: A purchaser's attorney, paid entirely by the purchaser, fails to pass the disclosure materials on to the purchaser. All required parties completed and signed the certification and acknowledgment language. What does 745.113(d) say?

options.A: The seller, lessor, or agent shall not be responsible for that failure
options.B: The seller is responsible and must repeat the disclosure
options.C: The seller's agent is responsible for the attorney's failure
options.D: The sale must restart with a new 10-day period

questions.explanation: "The seller, lessor, or agent shall not be responsible for the failure of a purchaser's or lessee's legal representative (where such representative receives all compensation from the purchaser or lessee) to transmit disclosure materials", provided all required parties completed and signed the language.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.113, Certification and acknowledgment of disclosure (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.topic: Keeping records, forms and electronic disclosure
questions.question: On EPA's page about real estate disclosures, what must be obtained when the disclosure is given electronically?

options.A: A paper copy signed by an EPA official
options.B: A notarized statement from the seller's agent
options.C: Approval from the State home inspector licensing board
options.D: Consent from the renter or buyer to show they can access the forms electronically

questions.explanation: EPA's page says: "If using electronic disclosure, must get consent from the renter or buyer to show they can access the forms electronically."

source.title: EPA: Real Estate Disclosures about Potential Lead Hazards (retrieved Nov 15, 2026)

questions.topic: Enforcement and State and local rules
questions.question: Under 745.118(e), failure or refusal to comply with 745.107, 745.110, 745.113 or 745.115 is a violation of which laws?

options.A: The Clean Air Act and the Clean Water Act
options.B: The Fair Housing Act only
options.C: 42 U.S.C. 4852d(b)(5) and TSCA section 409 (15 U.S.C. 2689)
options.D: Each State's home inspector licensing law only

questions.explanation: 745.118(e) says such failure or refusal "is a violation of 42 U.S.C. 4852d(b)(5) and of TSCA section 409 (15 U.S.C. 2689)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.118, Enforcement (as of Nov 12, 2026)

questions.topic: Enforcement and State and local rules
questions.question: A city ordinance requires sellers to give an extra local notice about known lead-based paint. What does 745.119 say about the federal subpart and that ordinance?

options.A: The federal subpart replaces the local notice requirement
options.B: Nothing in the subpart relieves the seller, lessor, or agent from responsibility for complying with it, and neither HUD nor EPA assumes responsibility for ensuring compliance with it
options.C: EPA ensures that sellers comply with the local requirement
options.D: Only the agent, not the seller, must comply with the local requirement

questions.explanation: "Nothing in this subpart shall relieve a seller, lessor, or agent from any responsibility for compliance with State or local laws" on lead disclosure, and "Neither HUD nor EPA assumes any responsibility for ensuring compliance with such State or local requirements."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.119, Impact on State and local requirements (as of Nov 12, 2026)
